title: Canonical descended omega and natural evaluation
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with field k and characteristic p, a prime l different from p, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l in an independent universe, and a separated finite-type scheme X over k. Use the actual raw rational finite stages, scalar extensions, tensor comparisons and common-stage pair category of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data]. For Finite F satisfying FiniteCoherent, use omega at the base coefficient stage, its inverse finite scalar u comparisons, and evaluation at the actual stage of each pair transported by tensorInclusion and descendedComparison. These explicit omega comparisons obey the scalar square and this explicit evaluation is natural in its contravariant argument. The finite-inclusion evaluation normalization follows by cancellation of the explicit tensor comparison.

source.place: Final coefficient-transport paragraph; core descent retained steps 1--5 and formal retract restriction step 10

proof.text: Express each descendedOmegaComparison through the finiteOmegaStageComparison and the stage transIso. The finite omega tower equation and transIso cocycle imply the base-origin omega square: cancel the base-to-E finite comparison, then use naturality of transIso. Finally conjugate by operationStageTransitionIso to recover the requested literal inclusionTransition square.

At a finite inclusion, precompose the desired evaluation naturality equation by the tensor inclusion followed by the dual comparison; it is an isomorphism. Tensor-inclusion naturality moves the finite arrow through, and descendedEvaluation_finite cancels the comparison factors. Naturality of descendedComparison and finite evaluation naturality identify the two resulting composites.

Prove the transition equation for descendedComparison by equality induction from the literal stage system and the representative formula for the descended contravariant morphism. Its finite comparison acquires operationStageTransitionIso on the finite dual and its contravariant correction on the input. The morphism-of-stage-systems coherence equation cancels the self-transition factors.

Precompose the evaluation equation for a stage transition by the included finite tensor scalar isomorphism and the two dual comparison isomorphisms. Tensor-inclusion scalar coherence identifies one side with included source evaluation followed by the omega comparison. The other side reduces by the normalized finite evaluation scalar square and the omega square proved above. This gives evaluation naturality along each transIso.

Every quotient arrow is isoToStage.hom followed by an included finite arrow followed by isoToStage.inv. Dinaturality is closed under composition by functoriality of tensor and contravariant duality, and under inverses of isomorphisms by cancellation. Apply the preceding inclusion and transition equations to the three factors. This proves naturality for every representative and hence every arrow.

lean.statement:
theorem descendedEvaluation_equations (F : Finite D l hl Ω X)
    (hF : FiniteCoherent D l hl Ω X F) :
    (∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L),
      (inclusion (Y := X) L).map (F.scalar E L h).omega.hom ≫
        (descendedOmegaComparison D l hl Ω X F L).hom =
      (inclusionTransition l Ω X E L h).hom.app
        ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) X).obj
          (F.omega E).omega) ≫ (descendedOmegaComparison D l hl Ω X F E).hom) ∧
    (∀ (K M : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X) (f : K ⟶ M),
      (CoefQbarTensor D l hl Ω X).map
          (Prod.mkHom f (𝟙 ((descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).obj (op M)))) ≫
        descendedEvaluation D l hl Ω X F hF M =
      (CoefQbarTensor D l hl Ω X).map
          (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 K) ((descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map f.op)) ≫
        descendedEvaluation D l hl Ω X F hF K)
